messages.subject: differents between lavaan 0.5-15 and 0.5-16
parts:
Hi everybody.

Today I refit my sem models using new version of lavaan

modelo <- "
# latentes
structural =~ c3_1 + c3_2 +c3_3 + csc
trust =~  d4_2 + d4_3 +d1 + d2
conf.gov =~ d6_1 + d6_2 + d6_3 + d6_4

#regresiones

structural ~  edad  +  edad.cuad  + sup_tot+party.rec + gestudPrimarios + gestudSecundarios + gestudUniversitarios + ingresos1+ comarca2 + comarca3 + comarca4 +  t8  + sucesion.recProbable.sucesion +  ownertitular.explot  
 

trust ~ structural  + edad.rec  + gestudPrimarios + gestudSecundarios + gestudUniversitarios + ingresos1 + f1  + tasa_paro_2011

conf.gov ~ trust + structural  + edad + edad.cuad + gestudPrimarios + gestudSecundarios + gestudUniversitarios + ingresos1 + t4.rec + f2  + f1 + tasa_paro_2011 + log.irpf



# covarianzas
d4_2 ~~ d4_3
d6_3 ~~ d6_4
"
fit.sem.ordinal2 <- sem(modelo,data=datos,std.lv=T,ordered=variables.medida)

where variables.medida are the variables in measure part of model. Well, in lavaan 0.5-15 I get a RMSEA of 0.032 but in lavaan 0.5-16 RMSEA is 0.6.  why is happening ? Anyway, I'll use old lavaan package until I understand what happens.

Regards

messages.subject: Re: differents between lavaan 0.5-15 and 0.5-16
parts:
On 03/18/2014 01:15 PM, José Luis Cañadas Reche wrote:
> Hi.
> Thanks for your time.
>
> I send a copy of part of my data and a small script. With lavaan 0.5-16
> rmsea is 0.631 and in previous version 0.036 . Both version have been
> installed from CRAN repository.

There is nothing wrong with the RMSEA. But the model has a terrible fit
in 0.5-16 (while much better in 0.5-15).

This is caused by the exogenous variable 'edad.cuad', which has a
variance of 2947001. Scaling this variable (say, by diving by 1000)
seems to solve the problem.

The difference between 0.5-15 and 0.5-16 is that the latter better shows
how unstable the solution is...

Yves.
